<thought>Analyzing the spectrum, the most prominent isotopic pattern is a relatively strong M+2 peak (~16 % of the monoisotopic intensity). This intensity is far higher than expected from 13C₂ contributions (~1 %) and matches the combined contribution of several 34S isotopes (≈4 % per sulfur atom). No clear 2 Da spaced 3:1 (Cl) or 1:1 (Br) patterns are present. Therefore, sulfur is the only element whose isotopic signature can be definitively identified.</thought>
<final_answer>['S']</final_answer>
